edit.description: Two encoders of one line. `render_shell_edge_findings` (:1081) and `render_manifest_findings` (:1675) each open with a preamble and then loop `out.push_str(&format!("\n  {}: {}", finding.rule, finding.message))` — the same statement at :1084 and :1685, the only two spellings of it in `src/` — and the first one's doc comment declares the twinning outright ('the same shape [`render_manifest_findings`] gives a manifest's, so the guard's one surface reads one way whichever edge speaks'). A self-declared shared shape held by two copies is the residue class: give the guard's in-band surface one encoder taking the preamble and the findings, and let `render_manifest_findings` keep only the job the other half does not have — picking its header by rule precedence (unparseable, then unreconstructable edit, then contract) before delegating. `render_shell_edge_report` (:1061) already calls the shell half per section and needs no change beyond the renamed callee.

summary: Two encoders of one guard finding line: the post-edge and manifest renderers each spell the `<rule>: <message>` line themselves.

tests.asserts: one diagnostic rendered under each edge's preamble produces the identical finding line, so the two edges cannot drift apart in shape; the manifest header precedence (unparseable over unreconstructable-edit over contract) still holds over a populated finding set

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the existing guard surface assertions in tests/it/install.rs and tests/it/cli.rs unchanged — the rendered bytes do not move — and one encoder in `src/install.rs` producing both edges' finding lines.
notes: Posture sweep at src/install.rs. Verified this tick: `rg -an '\\n  \{\}: \{\}' src/` returns exactly :1084 and :1685. Serialized behind the binding-limit fold, which rewrites the same renderers' headers — file-disjointness is unavailable and the two touch one seam.
